pages.title: App Discovery Errors
pages.body:
If **App Discovery** (the scan for new workspaces and new apps, reachable from the workspace list) reports errors, here's what they mean.

**"N workspace(s) could not be scanned"**

By far the most common cause: you're currently signed into a **different** Dropbox or OneDrive account than the one that owns those workspaces.

RacerX supports only one signed-in account per cloud provider at a time on a given device — one Dropbox account, one OneDrive account (you can be signed into both providers at once, just not two accounts on the *same* provider). If you sign out and sign back in with a different account on the same provider, any workspace that belongs to the account you just left can no longer be scanned — RacerX is asking that provider "what's in this folder?" using the wrong identity, and the provider correctly refuses.

This is expected behavior, not data loss: nothing about those workspaces is deleted or corrupted. Sign back in with the account that owns them and scanning works normally again.

**"Dropbox — not found" / "OneDrive — not found"**

This just means the scan didn't find any *new* apps for that provider — not that the provider itself is missing or broken. It's the normal, expected result once you've already added everything you use; there's nothing to fix.

**Still stuck?**

See **Sign-In Issues** in this section, or check which account is currently signed in via the small account icons at the bottom of the sidebar — hovering over the Dropbox/OneDrive icon shows the display name and email of the account currently connected.

pages.title: Debugging Sharing & Invites
pages.body:
Invite, share, and workspace-scan activity isn't shown live anywhere in the app yet — but every step is already logged to a table called `sharing_log`, on whichever device performed the action. Run this in **SQL Viewer**:

```sql
SELECT datetime(ts/1000,'unixepoch','localtime') AS at, message, is_error
FROM sharing_log ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 30;
```

**Run it on both ends when something looks wrong** — the sender's device logs the invite attempt and the cloud provider's raw response; the receiver's device separately logs its own workspace scan. A problem can be on either side, and each device only has half the picture.

**What a healthy invite looks like:** two log lines close together — `"inviting <email> (editor) to item/folder …"` followed by `"invite result — {…}"` with a real provider response (a Dropbox `access_type`/`invitee`, or a OneDrive `permission` object with a `roles` array). If you see that, the invite genuinely reached the cloud provider — a missing email or a recipient who can't find the workspace yet is a separate question from whether RacerX's own invite call worked.

**What a scan problem looks like** on the receiving device: lines like `"sharedWithMe — 0 shared folder(s) to check"` (the provider doesn't think anything's been shared with this account yet — check the sender's log instead), or `"apps/ missing or empty, skipping"` (the provider *did* report the shared folder, but RacerX's scan won't treat it as importable until it has at least one app folder in it).

**Sharing this with support:** this query's output is plain text you can copy and send — it's the same information Claude Code (or anyone else helping debug RacerX) would ask for first when a share or invite doesn't behave as expected. No need to describe what happened in your own words; the raw log usually shows it directly.

pages.title: Performance Tips
pages.body:
- Keep the app in the foreground when active collaboration is happening — background polling is less frequent for Messenger and paused for Wiki and Forms
- Large channels with many messages may take a moment to load on first launch as the full history is indexed
- Use the SQL Viewer to check how many records are in a table if a Forms app feels slow:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM records_{appId};
```
- If the app feels unresponsive, check your internet connection — cloud storage API calls require a stable connection
- On macOS: if you see the spinning beachball, switch away from and back to the app — this restores the window's event handling
